products.name: Discord
products.key_insight: Discord's behavioral design success comes from an unusual source: it's one of the few major platforms where the engagement loop is primarily social rather than algorithmic. There's no recommendation algorithm pushing content — engagement is driven by genuine community belonging and real-time social presence. The 'someone is typing...' indicator, voice channel presence, and @mention notifications create a sense of liveness that makes communities feel inhabited rather than archived. Discord's investment escalation (join → customize → earn roles → moderate → build bots) creates deep switching costs through identity investment rather than content lock-in. This makes Discord's engagement more ethically defensible than algorithmic platforms: users return because they have genuine social bonds, not because an algorithm has learned to exploit their attention patterns.
